title: Accept 11000150: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations
body:
## Accepted result and published preprint

**A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations**, Alec Kriebel. Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430927 (https://zenodo.org/records/23430927).

For each fixed genus g ≥ 1, let S(g,1) be an oriented compact surface with one boundary component, and let maps and isotopies fix that boundary pointwise. We prove that ordered positive factorizations of one positive boundary Dehn twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with repetitions permitted and pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. Their maximal length M(g) is finite and attained, with M(g) ≥ 4g(2g+1). Peripheral factors occur only in the singleton factorization; otherwise all factors are nonseparating. The values M(1) = 12 and M(2) = 40 are credited deductions from prior work with the convention bridge stated. This gives a complete negative answer, under the stated conventions, to the separately printed restricted arbitrary-length clause in the Wajnryb/Farb problem collection. The full original maximum and classification bundle remains partial: exact M(g) for g ≥ 3, explicit upper formulas, an effective exhaustive-enumeration stopping criterion, extremizers, and Hurwitz, positive Artin, T-move and A5/D6 classifications remain unresolved in this work. The note is a credited deduction and exposition. Cossu and Tringali's arXiv:2208.05869v3, Corollary 4.13, supplies the generic finite-alphabet finiteness corollary through a normal reduced cone and nonerasing atomic expansions. The support and ribbon arguments explicitly build on Juvan–Malnič–Mohar, Malestein–Rivin–Theran, and Cahn–Fanoni–Petri. Honda–Kazez–Matić, Smith, the chain relation, and Baykur–Monden–Van Horn-Morris provide credited premises. Exact historical priority of the resulting surface application, novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain UNKNOWN; a bounded literature audit is not an absence proof. Extensive AI tools were used in mathematical and source checking, writing, code, and package preparation. This preprint is unrefereed, has no external human peer review, and is not formally certified. The accompanying verification kit provides written proof and source/custody records plus reproducible finite fault controls; those controls do not replace the universal proof or replay omitted historical inputs.

## Accepted scope and review

For every fixed g≥1, positive boundary-twist factorizations with pairwise curve intersection≤1 and no disk-bounding factors form finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes; M(g) is attained and finite, with 4g(2g+1)≤M(g). Repeats allowed.

Arbitrary-length subquestion is answered negatively in fixed genus. Exact M(g) for g≥3, explicit upper formula and extremizer classification remain unresolved. This is possible eligibility for the literal boundedness subquestion, never a full resolution of the bundled maximum problem.

The result is accepted at the exact audited head `64b252b199f2692eef2545656190c14bcaf63889`. 4 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification.

The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1080_11000150`.

## Accepted boundedness partial, attempt 1/5

Problem 11000150 / AMR-109-0150, rank 1256. For each fixed genus g >= 1, positive factorizations of one boundary twist with pairwise geometric intersection at most one form finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes and have a finite attained length maximum. Repetitions are allowed, disk-bounding twists excluded, and all mapping classes preserve orientation and fix the sole boundary pointwise. The broader boundary-parallel convention is retained and analyzed.

The complete report and audit preserve the right-veering positivity argument, exact deletion algebra, self-contained finite-alphabet Higman proof, mod-two support bound, finite ribbon-graph/complement orbit proof and centrality step. The separating-factor exclusion includes the full capped Lefschetz-fibration construction, (-1) section and homologically nonzero fibre needed for the credited Smith theorem. Prior results are explicitly credited, including M(1)=12 and M(2)=40 and generic Higman-based factorization methods.

The arbitrary-length subquestion is answered negatively in fixed genus. The exact maximum for g >= 3, an explicit numerical upper bound and extremizer classifications remain unresolved. No Hurwitz, positive-Artin, T-move or A5/D6 classification is claimed. The distinct-support bound is not a factorization-length bound; no effective exhaustive-search stopping rule is supplied.

Full symbolic arguments and mathematical examples are retained. Programs, computational sections/results, fixtures, imported dataset contents, copied third-party source bodies and private coordination material are excluded. No excluded computation is rewritten as prose.

This AI-assisted, unrefereed edition claims no historical novelty, priority, current-openness certification, external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification. Recorded source retrieval and inspection are historical observations. Edition preparation makes no new scholarly retrieval, PDF rehash, source inspection or literature-search claim.

QUEUE.md and unrelated entries remain unchanged. Editorial preparation adds no substantive proof turn and does not reset attempt 1/5. No merge, release, DOI or outside outreach is requested.
